messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary rollout 2026-03-17T14:12Z - elevated 5xx rate in us-east-1. Abort criteria breached (5xx > 5% over 2m). Paging @emma on-call.

emma: acked — looking. can everyone post quick signal checks (5xx %, latency p95) and whether rollback/flag is possible immediately?

sanjay: saw spike in the canary pods only, not baseline. 5xx jumped from ~0.3% -> ~6.8% in last 90s. p95 latency up ~120ms. root cause not obvious yet. logs show repeated `model-runtime: kvcache-miss` exceptions on a subset of hosts.

liz: tagging customers likely hit: high-volume clients routed to canary (traffic-split 5%). rough calc -> ~1.8% of total requests see errors, some clients report >10% errors (support thread linked).

emma: OK trying abort path first — flipping rollout.flag.canary -> off. if that doesn't halt traffic within 30s, we'll rollback. can someone confirm feature-flag path and who has perms?

alice: i can flip. doing it now.

alice: /feature-toggle set rollout.flag.canary false (UI). ui shows success.

alice: :white_check_mark: toggle applied. routing controller logs: `route-reconciler: removed canary target from traffic-split`

sanjay: still seeing 5xx on those nodes, traffic is draining but pods still return 500 on new requests. might be warmup kvcache issue.

emma: can we redirect new traffic to baseline immediately? any quick routing override?

alice: issuing override to pin traffic to baseline group. `curl -XPOST https://infra/api/override -d '{"target":"baseline"}'` -> 202 accepted.

liz: monitoring customer-facing dashboard: status page shows error rate decreasing for most regions except us-east-1 where some pods keep serving errors.

sanjay: logs from one pod: ```
2026-03-17T14:13:02Z ERROR model-runtime failed to restore kvcache: invalid-kv-index
2026-03-17T14:13:03Z ERROR http: upstream 127.0.0.12:8080 respond 500 {"error":"kv cache corruption"}
```

emma: given partial draining + continued 5xx, i'm authorizing a rollback of this deploy across stages. alice/liz coordinate rollback. I'll also open a P0 incident doc.

alice: starting rollback job `deploy/2026-03-17-canary-7` -> initiated. deploy-bot: rollback started, wave=all, timeout=15m.

deploy-bot: Rollback job 7721 accepted. Staged rollback to baseline container image.

liz: contacting support to surface impacted customers and draft bridge note. ETA to close customer impact calc ~10m.

sanjay: quick mitigation idea: mark problematic nodes as tainted so autoscaler won't schedule, and restart runtimes after clearing kvcache. but that's more manual. Rollback is safer now.

emma: agreed — prioritize rollback. sanjay you and alice own pod-level remediation after rollback completes. liz own comms + support. i'll stay on this incident and escalate to eng-sre if rollback doesn't reduce 5xx within 2m of completion.

alice: rollback progress: 30% -> 75% -> 100%. deploy-bot: rollback complete.

sanjay: post-rollback metrics: 5xx back to baseline ~0.4% within 90s. p95 latency normalized.

liz: customer impact summary (prelim): ~2% of global requests experienced errors during 14:12-14:18Z window. Top impacted customers: acct-092 (10% error spike), acct-501 (8% spike). Support has opened tickets and issued temporary mitigation steps.

emma: posting incident doc link in #incidents and assigning postmortem. tagging eng-runtime for kvcache investigation.

pagerduty-bot: Incident 2026-03-17-4955554321 acknowledged by emma. Severity: P1 -> paging stopped.

alice: handing off to emma for on-call summary and postmortem assign. i'm going to run targeted restarts on nodes that showed kvcache errors after rollback.

emma: thanks all. next steps: (1) eng-runtime triage kvcache invalid-index errors (sanjay lead), (2) postmortem in 48h, (3) customer follow-ups by liz. leaving this thread open for any followups. :white_check_mark:
